skill.name: lark-approval
skill.description: Guide Lark and Feishu Approval API work for approval instances and task management with lark-cli.
skill.summary: Manage Lark approval instances and tasks through documented lark-cli operations.
skill.author: larksuite

security_audit.summary: Most external-command alerts are false positives from Markdown code fences, inline method names, and documented lark-cli usage. The filesystem finding is confirmed because SKILL.md instructs agents to read ../lark-shared/SKILL.md outside the skill package. A semantic risk remains because state-changing approval actions lack explicit confirmation guidance.

remediation.suggestion: Bundle the required shared authentication and permission guidance inside this skill, or vendor a reviewed local copy instead of referencing ../lark-shared/SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Write approval actions lack confirmation guidance
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before cancel, approve, reject, transfer, or cc actions, and show the target approval or task identifiers first.
Clarify that lark-cli examples are documentation and keep command arguments fixed or schema-derived to reduce false command-execution signals.

semantic_findings.title: State-Changing Approval Actions Lack Confirmation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md lists cancel, approve, reject, and transfer operations but does not require user confirmation before write actions. An agent following the skill could change approval state after an ambiguous request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented methods are clearly state-changing approval operations. The file provides schema guidance and scope mapping, but no explicit confirmation or dry-run guidance before write actions.

content.value_statement: Approval teams need precise CLI guidance for Lark workflow actions. This skill maps approval instance and task operations to schemas, commands, and required scopes.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to inspect approval API schemas before calls.
Documents approval instance operations for get, cancel, and cc.
Documents approval task operations for approve, reject, transfer, and query.
Maps each approval method to its required Lark permission scope.
Guides use of lark-cli for Lark Approval API requests.
limitations: Requires an installed and authenticated lark-cli binary.
Requires valid Lark app scopes for each requested operation.
Does not include full request schemas; users must run schema inspection.
Write actions can change real approval records and need confirmation.

use_cases.title: Review approval instance details
use_cases.description: Operations staff can prepare a safe lookup for a single approval instance before acting on it.

use_cases.title: Handle pending approval tasks
use_cases.description: Approvers can identify the correct task operation and required scope before approving, rejecting, or transferring work.

use_cases.title: Map API scopes for integration work
use_cases.description: Developers can match approval methods to Lark scopes when configuring app permissions and CLI requests.

prompt_templates.title: List approval options
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the available Lark approval instance and task operations. Include the required permission scope for each operation.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare instance lookup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me retrieve approval instance {{instance_code}}. Check the schema first, then explain the needed lark-cli approval instance operation and scope.

prompt_templates.title: Plan task action safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Approve, reject, or transfer a task
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a confirmation checklist for {{action}} on approval task {{task_id}}. Include schema checks, required scope, and fields to verify before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Design approval workflow automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a lark-cli workflow to query pending approval tasks, inspect schemas, route decisions, and require confirmation before any write action.

output_examples.input: I need to know which scope is required before querying approval tasks.
output_examples.output: The task query operation requires approval task read access. Inspect the schema first, then prepare the query with the correct user context.

output_examples.input: Help me cancel an approval instance.
output_examples.output: First verify the target approval instance identifier and your write scope. Then review the schema and ask for explicit confirmation before cancellation.

output_examples.input: What can I do with approval tasks?
output_examples.output: You can query task lists and prepare approve, reject, or transfer actions. Write actions require the approval task write scope and careful confirmation.

best_practices: Run schema inspection before every raw approval API request.
Verify app scopes and acting user context before write operations.
Confirm approval instance IDs, task IDs, and comments before execution.
anti_patterns: Guessing request fields without checking the schema.
Running cancel, approve, reject, or transfer actions without confirmation.
Putting Lark tokens, app secrets, or private approval data in prompts.

faq.question: What Lark approval resources does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers approval instances and approval tasks for the operations listed in SKILL.md.

faq.question: Does this skill include authentication setup?
faq.answer: It points to shared Lark authentication guidance, but the audited package does not include that file locally.

faq.question: Can it approve or reject tasks directly?
faq.answer: It documents the task operations and scopes. The user must provide valid identifiers, permissions, and confirmation.

faq.question: Why should I run schema inspection first?
faq.answer: Schema inspection confirms the expected parameters and data shape before calling the Approval API.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What is the main audit concern?
faq.answer: The skill references a parent-directory shared file and should be packaged with all required guidance included.
